claim: `'&'`-channel phase validation covers `defaultBinding` only, not bindings a tuning adds or an override substitutes
Shortcut lookup evaluates params thunks for bindings that have no displayable shortcut, and one can throw

triage.scenario: A variant with a keyboard binding and a pointer binding whose thunk needs pointer state; actionItemShortcuts runs the thunk early and it throws
triage.cause: params evaluated before the shortcut filter

claim: Adjusting an immediate last operation replays raw given params, so the current tuning changes params the form doesn't show

triage.scenario: Thunk tuning gives axis x; trigger; change the thunk to y; adjust distance in the panel; the replay uses axis y
triage.cause: immediate path doesn't capture resolved params

claim: pushOwner's release removes the newest copy of a value pushed twice, reordering the stack

triage.scenario: One value is pushed twice onto the same owner stack, for example a module-constant `BindingOverrides` map or `ActionTuning` that two components pass to `overrideBindings` / `tune` on one node. Another holder's value sits between the two. The stack is `[T(first), U, T(second)]`. When the first holder releases, `lastIndexOf(value)` removes index 2, which is the second holder's slot, leaving `[T, U]`. U now beats T, although the T still registered was pushed after U and should win: "a later one beats an earlier one in the same scope". The doc promises that "the release takes out *its own* entry wherever it now sits", but with equal values it cannot find its own entry.
triage.cause: release identifies its entry by value, not by a per-push token

claim: After an id change, drive sends the new action's input to the previous action's open control

triage.scenario: Open A with input; switch the id to B and call edit.input from a layout effect; A gets B's params and commits, and B never opens
triage.cause: effect ordering versus the latest-id ref

claim: A tuning's params never reach ctx.params of a UI-driven ongoing action begun without params

triage.scenario: `registry.tune('opacity.set', { params: { step: 0.1 } })`, then a control calls `begin('opacity.set')` with no params (or `useOngoingAction(...).input` before any value). The dispatcher starts the invoker with `uiInvocationCtx(deps, undefined)` (`dispatcher/uiOngoing.ts:92`); `wrapInvoker` lays the tuning only when `ctx.params` is set (`ctx.params ? { ...ctx, params: base(ctx.params) } : ctx`), so the action reading `ctx.params` — where the `InvocationCtx.params` doc says UI-driven actions get theirs — sees no tuned params on start, then sees them on the first `update` that carries params. The `ActionTuning.params` doc promises "params every invocation starts from". The same guard on `onMove` drops them for an update with no params.
triage.cause: tuning laid only over present params

claim: A merged tuning form loses the added form's name when the action's own form has no name

triage.scenario: an action's own `params` form has `name: ''`, which `PrefGroup` defines as "no heading". A tuning adds a `form` named "Brush". `formWith` returns `{ ...form, ...a, … }`, so own's empty `name` overwrites "Brush". The last-operation panel then titles the run `schema.name || action.label`, which gives the action's label instead of "Brush". This contradicts formWith's own doc: "named for `own` where it names itself".
triage.cause: spread lets an empty name win

claim: A hold made by holdPreview keeps the label of the descriptor it was made from, not the live one it follows

triage.scenario: `holdPreview(defaultAction)` is registered, and a consumer later registers a replacement under `action.id` with another label. `holdingLive` replaces the gates and invoker with the live action's but keeps `rest.label` from the hold, which is the original's label. The doc says the hold "follows whatever that registry resolves for `action.id`: its replacement". A keymap editor or a shortcut list showing the hold names the replaced action.
triage.cause: label copied once at construction, not taken from the live action

claim: Adjusting a gesture operation replays it even after its action is unregistered, muted or refused
`rankedDepRegistry` loses its rank when a caller passes `{ rank: undefined }`
A yoke member mounted under another `<ActionsProvider>` takes that provider's menu host instead of its yoke tree's

triage.scenario: `useYoke()` is called under ActionsProvider P1; a canvas `<InputScope yoke={yoke}>` sits elsewhere, under ActionsProvider P2 (the `Yoke` doc says members "can sit anywhere in the tree"). Its actions/deps/tool nodes hang on P1's tree, but `Provide` takes `useContext(MenuHostContext)`, which is P2's, before falling back to `nodes.actions.menuHost()`. Context menus and menu rows inside that canvas list and trigger P2's actions against P2's active scope, never the canvas's own. Expected: use the menu host of the tree the nodes belong to (`nodes.actions.menuHost()`), which already returns the root's shared host.
triage.cause: menu host chosen by React location rather than by the node's tree

claim: A tuning's params reach a UI-driven ongoing action's `start` but not the `onMove` each `update` drives
A last-operation rerun that throws is treated as having run: the original entry stays undone with nothing in its place
A variant key can equal another action's id, so a saved menu entry resolves to the wrong action

triage.scenario: Action `align` with variant `left` and a separate action `align:left` both get key `align:left`; resolveMenu matches the exact action id first and runs the separate action
triage.cause: generated variant key not unique against action ids

claim: An emptied yoke left as its parent's active child takes every read from the root
A mute made in an ancestor scope does not reach the canvas dispatcher's own-actions list
Dev deps Proxy throws on any undeclared string property, including the introspection ones (`toJSON`, `constructor`, `$$typeof`, `asymmetricMatch`)
holdPreview of a legacy-bag action with an `eligible` rule passes only `ruleCtx`, losing every other dep

triage.scenario: an action with no `requires` (so `depsFor` hands it the legacy fixed bag: selection, scene, history, view, activeTool, booleansAdapter) but with an `eligible` rule is wrapped by `holdPreview`. `holding` gives the hold `requires: [...(action.requires ?? []), 'ruleCtx']` = `['ruleCtx']`, so the hold's deps are built by `createActionDeps` from that list alone. On the press, `showPreview` calls `action.enabled` / `action.preview` with that bag; in dev the deps Proxy throws on `deps.selection` (enabled reads as `predicate-threw`, preview logs and shows nothing), in prod they read `undefined`. On release `invoker.run(ctx.deps, now)` runs without `scene`/`selection`. Expected: the hold gets the deps the action itself would get — the legacy bag plus `ruleCtx`, or the action's gates and run read through the action's own deps.
triage.cause: `requires` added where the action declared none flips it from the legacy bag to declared deps

claim: A mixed modifier/letter held-key alias lets Ctrl/Cmd+letter start the offhand tool and blocks the browser chord

triage.scenario: buildToolOffhandBindings([{toolId:'hand', key:['Shift','k']}]); Cmd+K starts the hand tool and prevents the browser default
triage.cause: mods relaxation applied spec-wide

claim: A binding override that does not parse warns again on every tree change, from every node
A kept run writes its resolved values as session params even when nothing was adjusted, masking an `under` tuning's later values
handleWith's proxy breaks on a frozen handle, so reading a method throws a TypeError

triage.scenario: Ongoing action returns Object.freeze({onMove, onEnd}); a param tuning wraps it; isEmptyOngoingHandle throws on the first method read
triage.cause: Proxy substitutes non-configurable, non-writable properties

claim: A hold's release runs the held action outside any catch, unlike every other run path
withRoleMods widens a binding for a role whose old keys only an earlier role's widening admitted

triage.scenario: An action declares role A with keys `['shift']` and role B with keys `['alt']`. Its binding is written with mods `{ shift: 'optional' }`, so it admits A's key and not B's. A tuning moves A to `['alt']` and B to `['ctrl']`. The loop handles A first: A's old key `shift` is admitted, so `allow('alt')` adds `alt: 'optional'` to `mods`. Then it handles B. The check `was.every((k) => admitted(mods, k))` reads that same mutated `mods`, so B's old key `alt` now passes, and `ctrl` is widened as well. Ctrl-drags now reach a binding that was never written for role B. Reverse the role declaration order and `ctrl` is not widened, so the result depends on the order roles are declared in.
triage.cause: the admitted check reads mods being widened, not the spec's own mods

claim: `<DepRank>` above an `<InputScope>` does not rank the sources registered inside it
Last operation reads and writes a nested `params` form's values by dotted path as one flat key
adjust stores session params for an action whose tuning `keep`s them, so they surface once that tuning is removed

triage.scenario: a tool's options tuning with `keep` is live for action X; the user changes a value in the last-operation panel. `adjust` calls `held.keep(...)` (correct) and also `this.remember(id, values)` unconditionally. `tuningsOf` hides the session tuning only while a `keep` tuning is present; after a tool switch releases that tuning, the stale session params come back and are laid over every `under` tuning (tool defaults) for the rest of the session. docs/unruled.md (round fourteen) rules that such an action "stores no session params". Expected: skip `remember` when a tuning of `id` keeps the params.
triage.cause: session write not gated on a keeping tuning

claim: The last operation outlives the input scope it ran in, and adjusting it reruns against the parent scope's deps
`checkEnabled` JSDoc names the wrong throw reason
`<ActionsProvider>` never tears its root node down, so a held last operation keeps observing history after unmount
An action without `requires` gets the legacy dep bag from `trigger` and an empty bag from the dispatcher
Last-operation wrap of an ongoing handle splits `this`: onEnd/replay run on the original, every other method on a spread copy
A hold's release re-asks `enabled` but not the `eligible` rule, so it runs an action the mode no longer allows
`ActionsRegistry.paramsOf` reads tunings from the node it's called on, while `trigger` runs at the active leaf
`holdPreview` runs the raw descriptor it was handed, so a mute or tuning of the action's id does not reach its hold
The last-operation wrapper seals history after an ongoing action's start instead of before, so an edit made in start coalesces with the gesture's later stops

triage.scenario: an ongoing action that declares `params` and whose handle has `replay`, and whose `start` writes its first edit straight to the history (no journal) with later moves coalescing into it. `invoker.start(ctx, opts)` runs first, then `watchEntry(stack)` calls `stack.seal()`, so the moves' edits can no longer coalesce into the entry `start` pushed: one gesture leaves two undo entries only because a history is present and the action declares `params`. The watch also never saw that first push, so the later coalesce or push marks it unclean and the operation is not kept either. The immediate path (`wrap`) seals before running; the ongoing path should seal before `start` too (the stack is already read before `start`).
triage.cause: seal ordered after start

claim: `ActionsRegistry.begin` skips the `eligible` rule and `enabled` that `trigger` and `preview` both ask
Held-key preview and release check enabled without the view id and with a made-up world point, unlike the dispatcher's admission

triage.scenario: Hold bound in view `detail` with enabled true only for `detail`; dispatcher admits it, but showPreview/checkEnabled get no view, so nothing previews and release does nothing
triage.cause: routing facts not carried into gate calls

claim: A menu host under `<Yoke>` lists and runs against the tree root's active scope, not the yoke's
Last-operation rerun ignores an immediate invoker's `'pass'` and the action's `eligible` rule
trigger reports true ("it ran") when the action's run threw

triage.scenario: `run` throws partway (say a missing dep in prod). The catch logs the error and falls through to `return true`. The contract in `registry.ts` says `trigger` returns whether it ran one, and lists every other failure as `false`. A palette or menu caller that treats `true` as "done" (closing, toasting success) reports success for a failed command. It should return `false` from the catch.
triage.cause: catch falls through to the success return

claim: Last-operation wrap of an ongoing action swallows a handle's `'pass'` from `onMove`, breaking drag hand-off
`ToolNode.snapshot` returns a new value on every call when no node in its chain owns a tool
Tuned, session and binding params merge shallowly, so a nested param group loses leaves

triage.scenario: an action's `params` form has a group, e.g. `fill.color` and `fill.opacity`. After a last-operation adjust, the session tuning holds the nested `{ fill: { color, opacity } }` (`remember` → `nestPrefValues`). A binding or `trigger` then passes `{ fill: { color: 'red' } }`, and `tunedParams` does `{ ...out, ...given }`, which replaces the whole `fill` object, so `fill.opacity` from the session or a tuning is dropped and the run uses the action's default. `lastOperation.withValues` sets values by leaf path, so the store does treat params as nested; the layering that feeds `run`, `paramsOf` and `invokedParams` does not.
triage.cause: shallow spread over nested param groups

claim: A hold runs its action with the params resolved at the press, so a thunked binding param changed while the key is held is not what runs
begin admits the child's action, but an inherited parent dispatcher starts the parent's implementation without its gate

triage.scenario: A nested InputScope with no dispatcher registers a different ongoing action at the same id; begin through the child starts the parent's action with the child's deps
triage.cause: dispatcher looks the id up again instead of using the admitted descriptor

claim: `withRoleMods` widens a binding that never admitted a role, when that role's declared keys are empty
A UI-begun gesture kept as last operation ignores `ctx.params`, so the panel shows, and replay receives, the wrong values
A grouped settings form's default change params use a dotted flat key while its values and the last operation are nested

triage.scenario: An `ActionSettings` whose schema has a group (leaf path `stroke.width`) and no `params` function. `read()` returns values nested as the groups nest, and menus and panels read them back with `prefValueAt(values, 'stroke.width')`. When that field changes, the default returns `{ 'stroke.width': v }`, a literal dotted key. The action is triggered with it, so an invoker reading `params.stroke?.width` (the nested shape that `read` and the last-operation keeper's `withValues` / `nestPrefValues` use) gets nothing, and the change is silently dropped. Only flat schemas work with the default.
triage.cause: default params not nested at the leaf path
